reason: Image-2 speaks directly to GLP-1 users' most-discussed fear—losing muscle and ending up 'skinny fat'—with an instantly readable visual contrast and a specific promise ('Lose the weight, not your strength'), whereas image-1's 'too many apps' convenience pitch is a weaker, more generic pain point and its 'cut' framing plus medication disclaimer feel mismatched.
researchFindings: GLP-1 forum users (r/Wegovy, r/OzempicWeightLoss, RealSelf) frequently worry about muscle loss, 'skinny fat', sagging ('Ozempic face/butt'), and feeling weak and tired.
DXA substudies show roughly 25-45% of weight lost on semaglutide/tirzepatide is lean mass; resistance training plus 1.2-1.6 g/kg protein is the widely recommended countermeasure.
Appetite suppression on GLP-1s makes hitting protein targets hard, so protein tracking is a key job-to-be-done.

Competing GLP-1 apps pitch on dose logging (Shotsy), protein tracking 'to protect muscle mass' (GLPme), peptides (Pep AI), or food databases (MyFitnessPal/Cronometer); few combine strength training with nutrition, leaving the muscle-preservation angle under-owned.

Reddit fitness users commonly juggle two apps (e.g., Hevy/Strong + Cronometer/MFP) and wish for an all-in-one, but they tolerate it—the fragmentation pain is real but less emotionally charged than body-composition fears.

(Not confirmed by this research; based on prior knowledge) Meta restricts before/after body imagery in weight-loss ads, so image-2's side-by-side bodies may carry some policy risk, though the stylized illustration and strength framing may reduce it.
